reason: The text describes God inflicting plagues upon Egypt through Moses to compel Pharaoh to release the Israelites. While the plagues do harm the Egyptian population (both elite and common people), the narrative presents the external divine force (God/Moses) as the agent of harm, not the elite attempting to hurt regular people. Pharaoh (the elite) is the target of divine punishment for refusing to free the enslaved Israelites, not an agent trying to harm regular Egyptians. The dynamic is inverse to the statement: external forces punish the nation to coerce the elite's compliance, rather than the elite initiating harm against regular people.
